correctness.rationale: The exact factorial formula matches Henzi–Law (9). With K=d²≫n, the normalizing logarithm differs from lambda=binom(n,2)/K by O(n³/K²); the empirical factorial term differs from (log 2) times the collision count by at most 3(1+log 2) triple occupancies. Uniform cell-mass bounds make the latter o_p(1) at bounded lambda and o_p(lambda) at diverging lambda. Graph factorial moments give Poisson(lambda J), and the exact collision variance yields C/lambda→J; analytic copula integration gives J=1+a²/2 and the stated amplitude. All quantifiers and excluded boundary cases are explicit. The packaged standard-library checker passed 2,011 additional finite-sample and numerical assertions; it is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Henzi and Law give the identical Dirichlet-one rank-martingale terminal statistic but analyze fixed grids and their mixtures. Classical Dirichlet formulae and birthday occupancy asymptotics are expressly credited. No inspected source establishes the combined large-grid nonuniform Poisson terminal-evidence limit and sharp squared-density-energy cutoff; the closest indexed finite-horizon four-cell calibration fixes d=2, while this result requires d→∞. Generic sparse-multinomial and Bayes-factor priority risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The theorem studies a natural and statistically consequential resolution parameter in an existing histogram e-value. It identifies the exact birthday-scale non-Gaussian null law and a smooth non-null model with a sharp L2 detection-vs-decay boundary, rather than a routine numerical constant. It also exposes why low expected occupancy can cause evidence to disappear under fixed alternatives to an iid multinomial model, directly motivating grid choice and warning against transferring that power behavior to empirical sequential ranks.
